{
  "title": "The Book That Returns",
  "world": "cinematic storybook realism — tactile, believable, gentle wonder",
  "cold_open": "Every ten years, a book returns to the same shelf, always untouched, always returned by a man who never seems to age.",
  "question": "Who is he, and why does time not touch him, even as the world around him changes?",
  "journey": "The librarian follows him through the decades, watching as he returns the same book each time, his face unchanged, his steps steady. She asks no questions, only watches. The book is always the same, its pages yellowed, its spine worn. Yet, when she opens it, nothing is written inside. Only the silence of forgotten stories. She begins to notice the same snowfall, the same season, always on the same day, as if time itself holds its breath.",
  "discovery": "One day, she finds a name in the margins — her own. A name she had never written, but now carries with her, as if it had always been waiting to be found. A faded ink blot beside it suggests someone else once touched the page, long ago.",
  "emotional_turn": "Tears well in her eyes as she realizes the book has been waiting for her all along, guiding her through time, keeping her connected to something she had long forgotten — herself.",
  "payoff": "The man smiles, nods, and returns the book to its place. The clock on the wall ticks forward, but for the first time, she feels time standing still. A faint whisper echoes through the library — her own voice, speaking words she had never heard before.",
  "after_image": "The book sits alone on the shelf, silent and waiting.",
  "hero_shot": "The librarian stands before the shelf, her hand hovering over the book, as the light from a single window bathes her face in golden warmth."
}
